source: Kaggle ieee-fraud-detection (IEEE Computational Intelligence Society / Vesta)
scope: Transaction-risk scoring only; no graph or clustering claim -- see graph_feasibility_finding.

graph_feasibility_finding.question: Could card1-6/addr/email/DeviceInfo support a shared-attribute entity graph the way device_fingerprint_id/instrument_hash do in the primary pipeline, or the way YelpChi's same-reviewer edge does?
graph_feasibility_finding.answer: No -- measured directly on this real file, not assumed.
graph_feasibility_finding.conclusion: These fields are coarse, anonymized/bucketed categoricals, not per-entity identifiers: the largest groups run into the tens of thousands, far past the 5,000-node case this project's own supernode_stress_test.py already found catastrophic, and -- unlike that stress test's synthetic injection -- there is no way to tell a real collision apart from a real identity link in this anonymized public data. Building ring edges from them would either explode (see docs on the supernode stress test) or, if degree-capped, still claim coincidence as identity. Left as ordinary classifier features instead.

split.strategy: chronological by TransactionDT; earliest 70% train, next 15% threshold selection, final 15% holdout

model.name: class-weighted XGBoost (native categorical support, no hand-rolled encoding)

interpretation.primary_measure: PR-AUC -- base fraud rate here is ~3.5%, far denser than ULB's ~0.17%, so accuracy is less distorted but still not the headline number.
interpretation.threshold_selection: Best F1 on validation only; holdout labels were not used to select it.
interpretation.review_capacity_policy: Top-k queues are evaluated at predeclared analyst capacities; ranking uses probabilities only, never holdout labels.
interpretation.limitation: Real e-commerce transaction data with genuinely richer features than ULB (Vesta-engineered aggregates, counts, time-deltas), but still one row per transaction with no usable entity-linkage key -- see graph_feasibility_finding. Cannot validate graph clustering or ring detection; only a conventional scorer.
